Xona Space Systems was founded in 2019 with a mission of supporting modern technology to operate safely in any environment. To that end, Xona is deploying the first commercial satellite navigation infrastructure needed to support intelligent transportation systems like self-driving cars. In the last two decades, satellite navigation has revolutionized many industries. With more than 6.5 billion enabled devices, Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) find utility in nearly all facets of modern life, from the source of time for our communications networks to the source of safety-critical positioning in civil aviation. Now, another revolution is on the horizon, one which promises disruption of transportation, mobility, and safety. 
Autonomous systems in the form of self-driving cars, autonomous aerial platforms, and mobile robotics are on the rise, targeting improved access to the mobility of people, goods, and services. This transformation is one whose complexity demands more than what navigation systems today can provide. Xona Space System’s PULSAR satellite constellation will address this gap by delivering ultra-precise and highly reliable positioning data, essential for the safe and efficient operation of these autonomous systems. By advancing beyond the capabilities of current GNSS technology, Xona's PULSAR system is poised to be a cornerstone in the infrastructure of the emerging era of autonomous transportation, ensuring higher standards of accuracy and reliability in a world moving towards greater automation and connectivity.
To date, Xona US has been the central location for development of the core mission and engineering of the PULSAR system. Xona Canada has established itself as a small centre for R&D and is developing service operations to support critical needs of the service.
Xona UK was incorporated in 2019. Its priority has been as a gateway to business development in the UK. This project serves to springboard Xona UK’s development as a centre for commercialisation-based testing and validation. Eventually it is our goal to host mission operations in the country, splitting the role across continents and mitigating risks to using only a single location. 
Xona Canada was also incorporated in 2019 and hosts the office of the CTO (Tyler Reid). Its operations have focussed on R&D projects such as ionospheric modelling and as a development centre for work in precise point positioning (PPP) and corrections service backend. Work is underway to grow the potential of our Canadian offices to include service operations.

entityDescription:
Mobile Monitoring is a system that combines water and air quality control with smart solutions that facilitate and streamline the analysis of collected data. Our product allows for a quick response to environmental pollution events and minimizes their impact. The Mobile Monitoring System consists of:
- IoT solution along with a monitoring and analytical platform
Devices for continuous monitoring of water parameters, such as: Buoys and measuring floats - control parameters like oxygen content, redox potential, pH, water conductivity, nitrogen, phosphorus, algae, chlorine, which are used as indicators to detect undesirable processes in water. Water buoys for detecting leaks of oil-derived substances. Water drones for precise pollution mapping and creating water quality maps. A mobile device for temporary measurement of water quality. Data from drones and measuring devices are transmitted in real-time to the analytical platform, which controls water parameters and informs about exceedances. The system performs automatic data analysis, notifying users of deviations from the norm, allowing for a quick response and taking action to prevent the spread of pollution or the occurrence of an ecological disaster. Continuous monitoring using measuring devices is crucial because water pollution is often detected too late, with visible consequences. Real-time monitoring is essential, and sometimes even constant monitoring may be insufficient. In cases where minor deviations do not clearly indicate dangerous events or the extent of pollution, water drones provide a two-dimensional water quality map. Mobile Monitoring is a solution for every entity involved in water monitoring. Potential Mobile Monitoring clients include ports, local governments, environmental protection agencies, and industrial plants, who are legally obliged to monitor water quality.

CGIAR is a global research partnership for a food-secure future. CGIAR science is dedicated to transforming food, land, and water systems in a climate crisis. Its research is carried out by 13 CGIAR Centers/Alliances in close collaboration with hundreds of partners, including national and regional research institutes, civil society organizations, academia, development organizations and the private sector.
For 50 years, CGIAR has been a leader in agricultural science and innovation for development. From specific food crops to water systems to policy, CGIAR’s Centers across the globe – working independently and together in partnership – have produced science that has brought benefits to hundreds of millions of the world’s poor.Today, the planet is facing escalating climate and biodiversity crises. Research in agriculture, food, land and water is more multi-disciplinary than ever before. We know much more about the interconnected nature of our food, land and water systems. Traditional funding models have shifted dramatically.The world has changed. And CGIAR is changing with it. CGIAR adopts a holistic view of the food system, from farm to fork, recognizing that many other systems influence it, and that our solutions should minimize trade-offs between increased agricultural productivity and climate and environmental goals.In 2019, CGIAR began a reform to better wield its combined expertise and resources across its Centers.
CGIAR’s Centers are independent legal entities and research organizations collectively home to more than 9,000 scientists, researchers, technicians and staff working in over 80 countries.Each Center has its own local footprint with a host country agreement granting privileges and immunities (including no liabilities for taxes), and each with its own external auditor. Although the Centers draw on the same pooled funding via the CGIAR Trust Fund, and have adopted certain shared policies and procedures, the Centers are governed by their own respective constitutive documents and boards.
The CGIAR System Organization is governed by theCharter of the CGIAR System Organization,and in collaboration with theCGIAR System Council, provides governance to the CGIAR System. The System Organization has an important role in facilitating and overseeing the development, effective and efficient implementation of the2030 Research and Innovation Strategy. The System Organization enters into agreements with the trustee of the CGIAR Trust Fund,Funders, Centers and other relevant entities for funding CGIAR Research and other activities of theCGIAR System.

description:
Founded in 2018 and based in Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany, ResearchConcept io GmbH (RC) specializes in research and development services and consulting services for international organizations, universities, public and private companies and the general public. Under the leadership of its founder, RC has an impressive track record in innovative research and model development, particularly in the areas of aerosol composition and climate modeling.
RC's expertise spans various areas, including the study of hygroscopic growth of aerosols through the ongoing development of the gas-liquid-solid aerosol equilibrium distribution model (EQSAM). In addition to climate modeling, RC also offers advanced point forecasts for solar radiation and atmospheric visibility, combining innovative aerosol composition models with artificial intelligence. RC has been actively involved in the CAMS team and is committed to improving the source codes of the atmospheric composition prediction system, IFS-COMPO. IFS-COMPO is used to produce the CAMS forecasts for the global distribution of aerosols and trace gases under the coordination of ECMWF. The collaboration extends across various projects, including CAMS2_35 and the HORIZON Europe project CAMAERA, since 2024.
The integration of AFB SolarTec Ltd in 2021 and the establishment of the uniWeather team in 2022 demonstrate the continuous growth and expansion of RC's areas of activity. With a highly motivated and experienced team, RC continues to help the public adapt to climate change.
